title: Need for Clarification on Statements made by the Leader of the Opposition
what_it_is: Need for Clarification on Statements made by the Leader of the Opposition

sections.label: Singh on Deros gate-crashing
sections.summary: Mr Singh said the Minister referred to meeting Deros and that he had said during the elections that the Minister gate-crashed Mr Faisal Manap's meeting.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: During the Ministerial Statement on Race and Religion by Minister Shanmugam on 14 October 2025, Mr Singh clarified by stating that: "I think the Minister started by referring to meeting Deros and I mentioned quite clearly during the elections that he gate-crashed the meeting that Mr Faisal Manap was having with someone else.

sections.label: Singh asked to reconfirm gate-crash
sections.summary: It appears either Mr Faisal told an untruth repeated by Mr Singh, or Mr Deros is lying, and Mr Singh is asked to reconfirm the gate-crash position.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On the face of things, it would appear that: either, one, Mr Faisal has told an untruth, which has been repeated by Mr Singh during the General Elections (GE) and now in Parliament; or two, Mr Deros is lying.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, can Mr Singh reconfirm that his position is that Mr Deros had "gate-crashed" the meeting?

sections.label: Singh calls Deros a nobody
sections.summary: Mr Singh said a nobody claiming demands of a political party requires considering factors, and that he did not know Noor Deros, who founded the Wear White movement in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: During the proceedings on the Ministerial Statement on Race and Religion, Mr Singh clarified that: "my own view on this is, when a nobody claims that there is a set of demands that he has of a political party, one has to think of a number of factors." He added that, "So, by dealing with it on 23 or 24 April, points made by a certain Noor Deros, who really, no one knows.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: I certainly did not know of him." Mr Singh's statement that Mr Deros was a "nobody" whom "really, no one knows" gives the impression that Mr Deros was not known to the WP, to Mr Faisal, or to any of the other WP candidates who attended the meeting.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: However, it has been publicly stated that: (a) Mr Deros founded the Wear White movement in 2014.

sections.label: WhatsApp message before meeting
sections.summary: A WhatsApp message showed the ustaz who invited Mr Noor Deros told Mr Faisal about one hour before the meeting that Noor Deros would be present.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The WhatsApp message showed that the ustaz who had invited Mr Noor Deros to a meeting with Mr Faisal had sent a WhatsApp message to Mr Faisal on 20 April, about one hour before the meeting in question, indicating that Noor Deros would be present.

sections.label: No arrangement to meet Deros
sections.summary: Neither Mr Faisal nor the Malay WP candidates arranged to meet Mr Noor Deros or specifically sought him out for his views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Neither Mr Faisal nor the Malay WP candidates arranged to meet Mr Noor Deros or specifically sought him out for his views.

sections.label: No promises for political support
sections.summary: At the 20 April meeting, no promises or undertakings were made by Mr Faisal or the WP Malay/Muslim candidates in exchange for political support from Mr Noor Deros.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: When the meeting took place on 20 April, I can reconfirm that no promises or undertakings were made by Mr Faisal or the WP Malay/Muslim candidates present, in exchange for political support from Mr Noor Deros during the elections.

sections.label: Gate-crashed word incorrect impression
sections.summary: The speaker says using "gate-crashed" may have wrongly implied Mr Noor Deros was uninvited, since he was invited by an ustaz delegated by Mr Faisal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In using the word "gate-crashed", I may have created an impression that Mr Noor Deros was not invited by anyone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: This would be an incorrect impression since I had confirmed later in the course of my response in this House to Member Saktiandi that Mr Noor Deros's presence at the meeting was at the invitation of an ustaz delegated by Mr Faisal.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim candidates did not know
sections.summary: Mr Faisal may have known of him, but the other Malay/Muslim candidates did not know of him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Well, Mr Faisal may have known of him, but the other Malay/Muslim candidates did not know of him.

sections.label: Gate-crashed statement and WhatsApp message
sections.summary: The speaker quotes Mr Singh's 14 October clarification and notes a WhatsApp message one hour before the meeting said Mr Deros would attend.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The original statement, which was stated in Mr Singh's clarification on 14 October, he said, "I mentioned quite clearly during the elections that he had gate-crashed the meeting that Mr Faisal Manap was having with someone else." So, "gate-crashed" actually implies that you are not invited and that really, you are not supposed to be there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But I think we have heard – firstly, today, that in fact, there was a WhatsApp message and the ustaz had shared with Mr Faisal Manap one hour before the meeting that Mr Deros would be present.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, would it be fair to say that it is wrong to say that Mr Deros gate-crashed that meeting?

sections.label: Message revealed on 21 October
sections.summary: The message that Mr Noor Deros was attending the meeting, sent to Mr Faisal one hour before, was only made known to the speaker on 21 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The revelation of this message that Mr Noor Deros was attending the meeting which was sent to Mr Faisal one hour before the meeting was only made known to me, I believe I mentioned it, on 21 October.

sections.label: Gate-crashed word not correct
sections.summary: The speaker says that understanding led to using "gate-crashed", but on reflection that word was not correct because Mr Deros said he was invited by the ustaz.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: That is how I phrased — or that understanding led me to use the word "gate-crashed".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But on reflection, that would not be a correct word to use, because it is quite clear that, and by Mr Deros' own statements in public that he was invited by the ustaz who Mr Faisal was in contact with.
